title: import: a lookup cell resolves a name across the whole target object, not within the row's own master reference, so a repeated detail name ("Advance 30%" on two contracts) fails the row with reference_ambiguous
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnPkgK6CWrJa6t7Fk5

## What happens (@objectstack 18.4.0, measured by HotCRM's Order to Cash browser pass on 2026-11-14)

HotCRM's invoice import sets both `crm_contract` and `crm_billing_milestone`. The billing milestone is a `controlled_by_parent` detail of the contract. When a cell names the milestone by title (for example "Advance 30%"), the import resolves that name across **every** `crm_billing_milestone` row. If two contracts each have an "Advance 30%" step, the row fails with `reference_ambiguous`, even though the row's own contract identifies exactly one of them. You can reproduce this with HotCRM's shipped `assets/import-templates/invoices.csv` once two contracts carry a step with the same name.

The record form's picker does narrow by contract (lookupFilters / dependent picker), so the form and the import disagree.

## Ask

When a lookup's target has a master_detail (or a declared dependent filter) whose master the same row also sets, the import resolves the name **within that master** first. Ambiguity is answered only inside that scope.

## Acceptance

1. Two masters each have a detail named X. An import row that sets master A and detail "X" resolves A's X. The same holds for B.
2. A row with no master cell keeps today's behaviour (whole-object lookup, `reference_ambiguous` on a tie).
3. A name absent under the row's master answers `reference_not_found`, not a match under another master.
4. The import mapping docs and the data skill describe the scoping.

## HotCRM side

Until this ships, HotCRM's docs tell importers to use the step's record id when step names repeat across contracts.
